strongest_adverse_test: Author physical20 expressly adopts differences in absolute household SARs as the effectiveness measure. Physical23 accurately introduces the descriptive rates, then makes its own inferential step. It does not expressly claim that the paper authors reached the adjusted no-protection conclusion. Calling the omission of another analysis a source-description error would require an interpretive attribution not established by the quoted sentence.
reasoning: The categorical inference is statistically under-supported: crude equality cannot identify no vaccine effect when groups differ. But that defect is not equivalent to proving the actual Omicron risk claim false, and an adjusted observational association does not establish a definitive causal counterclaim. The user explicitly excludes missing evidence and policy/methodological disagreement as proven errors. Retain an unresolved source-use/inference lead with this boundary, rather than a provisional major finding based solely on omitted adjustment.
what_review_does_not_establish: No clinical efficacy, current transmission rate or causal effect is estimated here.
No conclusion about mandate necessity, proportionality or patient-protection magnitude.
No intent inferred and no author response invented.
